in_arabic.name: سبر
in_arabic.long_meaning: صبر (sabar) - to endure, to be patient, to persevere, to remain steadfast, to withstand, to tolerate, to bear, to wait, to be forbearing, to be steadfast in the face of adversity. It is also used to describe someone who is patient and enduring.

in_urdu.name: صبر
in_urdu.meaning: صبر (sabr) - shikwa (complaint), wajd (yearning), shauq (passion), rujhan (determination), mazloomiyat (oppression), sakht (difficulty), khudrat (power), qudrat (ability), rizq (provision), husn-i-zindagi (good living), hidayat (guidance)
in_urdu.long_meaning: صبر (sabr) - شکواء (shikwa) - a complaint, a lamentation, an expression of grief or sorrow. It can also mean 'yearning', 'passion', 'determination', 'oppression', 'difficulty', 'power', 'ability', 'provision', 'good living', or 'guidance'. Sabr is a virtue that is highly praised in Islam and is considered a necessary quality for a successful and contented life.

in_hindi.name: सबर
in_hindi.meaning: सबरी (sabari) - शक्ति (shakti) - power, strength, endurance, patience
in_hindi.long_meaning: सबर (sabar) - सबरी (sabari) - शक्ति (shakti) - power, strength, endurance, patience. In Hinduism, Sabar is a name of Lord Shiva and is considered to be a symbol of divine power and strength. In Sanskrit, the word 'sabar' means 'enduring', 'steadfast', or 'patient'.

in_pashto.name: سبر
in_pashto.meaning: سبر (sabr) - پیغام (pigham) - message, news, tidings, instruction, advice
in_pashto.long_meaning: سبر (sabr) - سبر (sabr) - پیغام (pigham) - message, news, tidings, instruction, advice. In Pashto, the word 'sabr' can also mean 'message', 'news', 'tidings', 'instruction', or 'advice'. However, in the Islamic context, it is used to mean 'patience' or 'perseverance'.
